candidate_relations.reason: There is no imaging or clinical syndrome of acute pulmonary embolism.
Treated pulmonary tuberculosis 10 years earlier is historical, not the atrial conduction diagnosis.
Lung cancer is not shown; the malignancy is metastatic bladder carcinoma.
There is no evidence of active tuberculous cardiac involvement as the primary diagnosis.
Exertional breathlessness with grade III diastolic dysfunction is an associated cardiac state, not advanced IAB/Bayés.
Hypertensive heart disease is not documented as the mechanism of the P-wave abnormality.
Atrial tachycardia is the tachyarrhythmia limb of Bayés syndrome but omits advanced interatrial block.
There is no effusion or tamponade physiology.
Metastatic bladder carcinoma with possible cardiac involvement is comorbidity/speculation, not IAB/Bayés.
The tracing is described as irregular NQT with atrial rate 210/min, more consistent with atrial tachyarrhythmia/flutter than typical AF, and it omits IAB.
Grade III diastolic dysfunction is an echocardiographic accompaniment, not Bayés syndrome.
Cardiac amyloidosis is a restrictive differential not established here.
Metastatic bladder carcinoma is the oncologic history, not the ECG diagnosis.
Diastolic heart failure is a related functional state, not IAB.
Carcinoid heart disease is a right-sided valvular disease, not IAB.
Atrial flutter is a related atrial tachyarrhythmia of Bayés syndrome but omits advanced IAB.
Cardiac involvement by metastatic bladder cancer is unproven and is not the IAB diagnosis.
Tuberculous pericarditis is not shown.
Prominent y descent raises constrictive pericarditis as a related consideration, not advanced IAB/Bayés.
Cardiac involvement in metastatic cancer remains an association, not Bayés syndrome.

case_quality_flags: Post-cardioversion P waves of 160 ms that are notched/negative inferiorly with atrial tachyarrhythmia constitute advanced IAB/Bayés syndrome; no candidate names IAB or Bayés.
